Amal — thanks, got the worksheet and matrix. Looping in Kimberly (solutions) and Jonas (enterprise eng) to provide the technical mapping and RBAC detail. Quick answers up front:
- Multiple SCIM endpoints: supported via per-tenant SCIM connectors (each tenant can have an independent SCIM base URL and token).
- SCIM PATCH & bulk: Redwood SCIM v2 supports PATCH (RFC 7644) and batch create via the bulk endpoint for initial provisioning; rate limits apply per connection.
- Delegated admin: tenant-scoped admin roles are supported (granular scopes: user_mgmt, group_mgmt, audit_read).
- Audit logs: provisioning events retained 365 days by default for Dedicated/Private plans; hosted can be extended via the observability add-on.

We'll follow up with a short document and a sample CSV mapping. Can you confirm whether Olive plans to have separate IdPs per business unit or a single IdP with multiple group scoping? That will affect the provisioning topology.

Hi Amal / Maya —

Adding the technical specifics requested below and attaching a short PDF with sample mappings. Key details:

1) SSO (SAML / OIDC)
- Both SAML 2.0 and OIDC are supported. For SAML we accept standard assertions up to 64KB; large attribute payloads should be minimized (NameID + 6 core attributes recommended).
- OIDC: we support custom claims in the ID token and userinfo; we recommend claims in userinfo for large attribute sets.
- You can configure multiple IdP connections per tenant; each connection can be bound to a subset of groups via the mapping rules engine.

2) SCIM provisioning
- SCIM v2 compliant endpoints. Supports PATCH (add/replace/remove), POST for bulk initial imports, and GET with pagination.
- SCIM filtering: eq, startsWith, and complex filters for group membership queries.
- Group handling: groups are first-class; we support nested groups up to 2 levels for RBAC assignment.

3) RBAC & admin controls
- Built-in roles: Org Admin (full), Tenant Admin (tenant-scoped user/group management), Support Analyst (read-only + escalate), Billing Admin (billing view + invoices).
- Custom roles: create role templates and attach granular permissions. Inheritance: tenant admin <— can be granted subset of org admin via templates.
- Delegation: yes — you can create delegated admin accounts scoped to specific tenants or group prefixes.

4) Audit & evidence
- Provisioning and SSO events are logged with actor, timestamp, source IP, and correlation id. Exportable via API or delivered to your SIEM (Syslog/HTTP). Default retention: 365 days for Dedicated/Private; hosted 90 days (extendable).

Attachments referenced: redwood-iam-overview.pdf (contains sample SAML responses, SCIM PATCH examples, role matrix).

Next steps: Maya / Jonas will provide a sample attribute-to-claim mapping and a recommended SCIM topology based on your answer about IdPs per BU.

Amal / team — technical addendum from infra/serving side:

- Multi-tenant topology options:
  a) Per-tenant SCIM connectors (recommended for strict BU isolation). Each connector has its own service token and can be rotated independently.
  b) Single SCIM connector with group-scoped mappings (lower operational overhead, recommended if IdP is shared).

- Rate limits and throughput: each SCIM connector has a per-minute call quota; bulk imports are rate-limited and we recommend using the bulk endpoint overnight for large imports (>50k users).

- Provisioning lifecycle hooks: we support pre-provision validation webhooks (your system can accept/deny creates) and post-provision callbacks for downstream sync.

- RBAC enforcement at API layer: all SCIM calls are validated against delegated admin scopes. For example, a tenant-level admin with user_mgmt scope cannot update Org-level billing attributes.

- Service accounts & keys: for automation, create a service account per connector with limited scopes; tokens can be rotated and audited.

Neha — can you confirm the default group cardinality (we typically cap nested group expansion at 50k members to protect performance) and whether we should propose an alternative?

-Jonas
